metadata.title: RDS MySQL Upgrade Assistant - Threat Model

businessContext.description: RDS MySQL Upgrade Assistant - An open-source CLI tool and MCP server that automates batch Blue/Green deployment upgrades for Amazon RDS MySQL 8.0 to 8.4.

components.name: Shell Scripts (AWS CLI)
components.description: 11 bash scripts that interact with AWS CLI for RDS operations and mysql client for database connectivity checks

components.name: MCP Server (Python/FastMCP)
components.description: Thin Python subprocess wrapper that exposes shell scripts as MCP tools for Kiro IDE/CLI interaction via stdio

components.name: Amazon RDS MySQL
components.description: Target RDS MySQL 8.0 instances and clusters being upgraded to 8.4 via Blue/Green deployments or in-place upgrades

components.name: AWS Secrets Manager
components.description: Stores database credentials (username/password) retrieved by scripts for MySQL connectivity

components.name: AWS IAM
components.description: Provides authentication for AWS CLI calls and optional IAM database authentication for MySQL connections

components.name: Kiro IDE/CLI
components.description: AI-powered IDE and CLI that communicates with MCP server via stdio to orchestrate upgrade workflows through natural language

connections.description: Shell scripts call AWS CLI which authenticates via IAM
Shell scripts retrieve database credentials from Secrets Manager
Shell scripts manage RDS instances via AWS API
Kiro communicates with MCP server via local stdio pipe
MCP server invokes shell scripts as local subprocesses
Shell scripts connect to MySQL for prechecks and validation using TLS

threats.threat_source: An attacker with local process access on the developer workstation
threats.prerequisites: with ability to intercept or modify MCP stdio communication
threats.threat_action: inject malicious tool calls through the MCP stdio pipe to execute unauthorized operations
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized RDS operations executed through the MCP server

threats.threat_source: An operator misconfiguring batch upgrade parameters
threats.prerequisites: with access to batch configuration files
threats.threat_action: configure high concurrency targeting all instances simultaneously causing service degradation
threats.threat_impact: simultaneous downtime across multiple production databases during upgrade

threats.threat_source: A malicious operator performing unauthorized upgrades
threats.prerequisites: when upgrade scripts lack comprehensive audit logging
threats.threat_action: perform destructive operations (switchover, cleanup) without traceable audit trail
threats.threat_impact: inability to attribute or investigate unauthorized database modifications

threats.threat_source: An operator or attacker with access to script debug output
threats.prerequisites: when bash debug mode (set -x) is enabled during script execution
threats.threat_action: capture credentials from debug trace output when scripts retrieve secrets
threats.threat_impact: exposure of database passwords and IAM auth tokens in log output

threats.threat_source: A malicious insider or attacker with filesystem access
threats.prerequisites: with write access to the script directory on the execution host
threats.threat_action: modify shell scripts to inject malicious commands that execute during upgrade operations
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized modification or deletion of production RDS instances

threats.threat_source: A local user or attacker on the execution host
threats.prerequisites: with access to process listing or shell history on the execution host
threats.threat_action: observe database credentials passed via -p CLI argument in ps output or bash_history
threats.threat_impact: exposure of database credentials enabling unauthorized database access

threats.threat_source: An attacker with access to script output or log files
threats.prerequisites: when error handling exposes raw AWS API responses
threats.threat_action: trigger error conditions to extract AWS account details from error messages
threats.threat_impact: disclosure of AWS account IDs and ARNs aiding further reconnaissance

threats.threat_source: A network-level attacker with a rogue CA certificate
threats.prerequisites: with network position to perform MITM on MySQL connections
threats.threat_action: intercept MySQL connections using ssl-mode=REQUIRED without CA certificate pinning
threats.threat_impact: credential theft or data interception during precheck/validation queries

threats.threat_source: An attacker who can modify batch configuration files
threats.prerequisites: with ability to modify YAML config files consumed by batch_upgrade.sh
threats.threat_action: inject malicious values into batch config YAML parsed by shell without full validation
threats.threat_impact: command injection or unintended operations on RDS instances

threats.threat_source: An authorized user with excessive IAM permissions
threats.prerequisites: with IAM credentials that have overly broad RDS permissions
threats.threat_action: use upgrade scripts to modify or delete RDS instances beyond intended scope
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized upgrade, modification, or deletion of production databases

mitigations.content: Use AWS Secrets Manager (--secret-id) or IAM database authentication (--iam) instead of -p CLI password flag. Credentials written to --defaults-extra-file with umask 077 and unset from memory.
Sanitize error messages to remove raw AWS API output. Error messages show generic guidance without exposing ARNs, account IDs, or internal API details.
Validate all inputs from batch config YAML and CLI arguments. Enforce regex patterns for instance IDs, version numbers, port, and region codes.
Enforce TLS for all MySQL connections using --ssl-mode=REQUIRED. Consider upgrading to --ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY with RDS CA bundle for full certificate validation.
Batch orchestrator enforces configurable concurrency limits (default: 3). Precheck gating automatically skips instances with errors. Dry-run mode validates before execution.
Add comprehensive audit logging to all upgrade scripts. Log timestamp, user, operation, instance ID, and outcome to a dedicated log directory with restricted permissions.

Apply least-privilege IAM policies. Separate read-only permissions (discover, precheck) from write permissions (upgrade, switchover, cleanup). Use IAM condition keys to restrict operations to specific instances.
Implement script integrity verification using SHA-256 checksums before execution. Verify minimum tool versions for aws, jq, mysql dependencies.
